import numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use("Agg"); import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
n = np.arange(1, 41)
k = n.astype(float)
geo = np.cumsum(2.0**-(k - 1))
p2 = np.cumsum(1/k**2)
alt = np.cumsum((-1.0)**(n + 1)/k)
har = np.cumsum(1/k)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 4))
for y in [2.0, np.pi**2/6, np.log(2)]:
    ax.axhline(y, color='gray', lw=0.8)
ax.plot(n, geo, 'o-', ms=3, lw=0.8, label=r'$\sum 2^{-(k-1)}\to 2$')
ax.plot(n, p2, 's-', ms=3, lw=0.8, label=r'$\sum 1/k^2\to\pi^2/6$')
ax.plot(n, alt, '^-', ms=3, lw=0.8, label=r'$\sum (-1)^{k+1}/k\to\log 2$')
ax.plot(n, har, 'd-', ms=3, lw=0.8, label=r'$\sum 1/k$ (diverges)')
ax.plot(n, np.log(k) + 0.5772156649, 'k--', lw=0.8, label=r'$\log n+\gamma$')
ax.set_xlabel('number of terms $n$ (dimensionless)')
ax.set_ylabel('partial sum $S_n$ (dimensionless)')
ax.legend(fontsize=8, loc='upper left')
plt.savefig("series_partialsums.pdf", bbox_inches="tight")

import numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use("Agg"); import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
n = np.arange(1, 41)
alt = np.cumsum((-1.0)**(n + 1)/n)
terms = []
for j in range(1, 20):
    terms += [1/(2*j - 1), -1/(4*j - 2), -1/(4*j)]
R = np.cumsum(terms)[:40]
L = np.log(2)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 4))
ax.fill_between(n, L - 1/(n + 1), L + 1/(n + 1), color='gray', alpha=0.2, label=r'$\log 2\pm 1/(n+1)$')
ax.plot(n, alt, 'o', ms=4, label='alternating harmonic')
ax.plot(n, R, 's', ms=4, label='rearrangement')
ax.axhline(L, color='C0', lw=0.8)
ax.axhline(L/2, color='C1', lw=0.8, ls='--')
ax.set_xlabel('number of terms $n$ (dimensionless)')

import numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use("Agg"); import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
n = np.arange(2, 51).astype(float)
fig, (a1, a2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(6.5, 3))
a1.semilogy(n, n + 1, 'o', ms=3, label=r'$\prod(1+1/k)$')
a1.semilogy(n, (n + 1)/(2*n), 's', ms=3, label=r'$\prod(1-1/k^2)$')
a1.semilogy(n, 1/n, '^', ms=3, label=r'$\prod(1-1/k)$')
a1.set_xlabel('number of factors $n$ (dimensionless)')
a1.set_ylabel('partial product (dimensionless)')
a1.legend(fontsize=7)
sieve = np.ones(600, bool); sieve[:2] = False
for i in range(2, 25):
    if sieve[i]:
        sieve[i*i::i] = False
primes = np.nonzero(sieve)[0][:100].astype(float)
P = np.cumprod(primes**2/(primes**2 - 1))
a2.plot(np.arange(1, 101), P, '.-', ms=3, lw=0.6)
a2.axhline(np.pi**2/6, color='k', ls='--', lw=0.8, label=r'$\pi^2/6$')
a2.set_xlabel('number of primes used (dimensionless)')
a2.set_ylabel('partial Euler product at $s=2$')
a2.legend(fontsize=8)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig("series_products.pdf", bbox_inches="tight")
